## Natural history notes

A medium to large centipede characterized by its flattened reddish-brown to orange body, many long legs, and enlarged rear legs that give it the “big-leg” appearance. In Florida, the Big-leg Centipede is part of the native centipede fauna, with records including north Florida and broader reports from the state, where it occurs in forested or semi-forested habitats under logs, bark, stones, leaf litter, and other moist cover. It is a nocturnal predator of insects and other small arthropods, using venomous forcipules to seize prey, and should be left undisturbed because larger centipedes can deliver a painful defensive bite.
